subject: English Language
content:
Compare writers’ ideas and perspectives, as well as how these are conveyed, across two or more texts. This includes: 
- Comparing the writers’ similar thoughts and feelings about a topic (e.g., nature).
- Comparing the methods they use to convey their thoughts and feelings (e.g., language features, structural choices, tone).
- Supporting responses with references to both texts.

Assessment focuses on:
• Appreciation and admiration for the natural world.
• Positive or troubling relationships between humanity and the natural world.

Methods to analyse may include:
• First-person narratives/observation of nature.
• Descriptive approach – literary style.
• Whole text structure – shifts between observation and description.
• Use of verb tenses – switching between past and present.
• Tone – objective but with personal enthusiasm.
• Language features – sensory and figurative language (e.g., alliteration, sibilance, onomatopoeia).
• Word choices.

subject: English Language
content:
Communicate clearly, effectively, and imaginatively, selecting and adapting tone, style, and register for different forms, purposes, and audiences. Organise information and ideas, using structural and grammatical features to support coherence and cohesion of texts.

Assessment includes:
• Matching tone, style, and register to purpose and audience.
• Using structural features (e.g., paragraphs, discourse markers) for coherence.
• Crafting linguistic devices and ambitious vocabulary for effect.

subject: English Language
content:
Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose, and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. This constitutes 20% of the marks for the specification as a whole.

Assessment focuses on:
• Sentence demarcation and punctuation accuracy.
• Use of Standard English and grammatical structures.
• Spelling accuracy, including complex and irregular words.
• Sophisticated and varied vocabulary.
